newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 6.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- Gold shares tumbled four percent on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Wednesday, bringing sectoral losses to 8.3 percent in two days as the bullion price dropped more than $5 an ounce.
- The Post Office has received government backing to raise the price of a standard letter by over 40 percent from April 7.
- Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals and his deputy, James Cross, dismissed fears that a surge in the money market shortage was due to large-scale foreign exchange outflows.

- The cabinet has decided to change the maintenance grant system for deserted mothers. It will be scrapped over the next five years and replaced with a child-support system to help support three million poor children.
- Former security police informers, allegedly including high-profile members of the current government, could be investigated by the "truth commission", its chairman Archbishop Desmond Tutu said.

- Chemicals manufacturer Sentrachem would report a loss in the six months to February as the costs of ill-judged forward exchange contracts by subsidiary Sanachem last year and a major restructuring of the troubled division had eaten into earnings, the group said.
BUSINESS REPORT

- Environment Deputy Minister Peter Mokaba said the government would not be blackmailed by a threat of 250 million rand in litigation costs over a 12 billion rand contract with Dubai-based Dolphin group to lease Mpumalanga province's nature reserves for 50 years.
- The World Bank launched the longest-dated Eurorand bond to date on Wednesday, with 2.5 billion rand of 20-year zero-coupon bonds announced by lead manager Hambros Bank.

- Sentrachem, the 4.9 billion rand a year industrial and agricultural chemicals group, will post first-half losses this year because of 261 million rand in extraordinary costs which will lop 134 cents off the earnings per share, the company said.

- Commercial banks were gradually replacing the Reserve Bank in the forward currency market, which was part of the reason for the high money-market shortage over the past few months, banking officials said.
SAKE-BEELD
- Chemical group Sentrachem suffered a loss of 261 million rand in the six months to end-February resulting from write-offs by Sanachem, one of its main subsidiaries.
- New vehicle sales continued their upward trend in February, but the market for light commercial vehicles dropped in a fall ascribed to drought in several summer rainfall areas.
- The South African Chamber of Business (Sacob) Business Confidence Index rose 0.9 points last month to 113.2, following January's 1.0 percent increase.
BEELD

- Television staff at the South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC) have been told that rationalisation consultants have recommended the scrapping of morning television programme GMSA, SABC programme manufacturer Safritel, the dubbing department and language unit by the end of April. The SABC has not yet taken any decision on the matter.
THE STAR

- Big businesses, which make up 80 percent of the postal system's annual mail volume, are incensed by the announcement of stiff tariff increases, with the post office saying it will increase the price of mailing standard letters by 43 percent.
- A spokesman for the state broadcaster, SABC, said close to 130 different ideas have been suggested for improving efficiency and saving costs.
